framing: He Was Socrates is not a privacy posture — it is a $0/month operating bill. Every component (bust UI, STT, TTS, inference, weights, persistence, distribution) sits on a free tier or the user's own silicon, so a school district adopting it pays the same as a single curious learner: nothing recurring.
target_persona: Public-school district IT procurement officers, NGO education leads, and bootstrapped indie devs who must justify every recurring SaaS line item — for whom 'cloud LLM tutor' is a non-starter at $0.06/1K-token × 30K students × 9 months.
primary_surface: Static-first single-file HTML preview hosted on GitHub Pages (Two-Weeks-Team org, $0); cost-ledger wireframe with dashed-box components and per-line $0 stickers; comparison panel pricing the cloud equivalent at ~$5.4K/mo for a 5K-seat district.
opus_4_7_capability: Long-context cost-totaling reasoning — Opus 4.7 cross-references the 6 frozen invariants, the entitlements file, and PR-Λ bench JSON to assemble a verifiable BOM where every $0 line item has a source-of-truth citation (entitlements, MLX cache, AVSpeech, SFSpeechRecognizer, Core Data, GitHub Pages free tier).
mvp_scope: Single self-contained HTML cost-ledger wireframe: 7 dashed-box components (Bust UI · Gemma 4 weights · MLX inference · STT · TTS · Wondering log · Distribution) each stickered $0; a 'Monthly Bill' panel summing to $0.00; a 'Cloud Equivalent' comparison panel itemizing GPT-4o + ElevenLabs + Whisper API + Pinecone + Vercel Pro to ~$5,403/mo for 5K seats.
one_liner_pitch: A Socratic tutor whose monthly bill is $0.00 — every line item is the user's own Mac, every cloud equivalent costs a school district $5K/mo it does not have.
